Mrs. Sallie G. Jones, who has been employed in the Indian Bureau
of the Interior Department for a period of four years, may be promoted
without examination under the civil service rules.
Mrs. Jones has been employed in the Interior Department in various
capacities since May, 1900. Her record for efficient and faithful service
is good. She was placed in the classified service under an Executive
Order issued October 9, 1908, and appointed copyist at $720 per annum.
In October, 1910, she was promoted to $900, and in April, 1914, in view
of the meritorious service which she was rendering, the Commissioner of
Indian Affairs promoted her to a clerical position at $iooo per annum.
However, owing to a ruling of the Civil Service Commission that under
the provisions of the Executive Order placing her in the classified service,
she wvas not eligible for promotion to said grade without examination, she
wvas, on August 16, 1914, reduced to $900 per annum.
Mrs. Jones is the widow of Robert Tyler Jones, a grandson of Presi-
dent Tyler, who was born in the White House during the administration
of President Tyler, and wvho, it is stated, wvas the only male child ever born
in the White House.

mended by the Director of the Census, who states that Mr. Brett's
experience in connection with the various machines used in the Bureau,
his familiarity with the matter to be tabulated, and his general education
are believed to he such as to fit him for clerical duties, and that his services
have always been satisfactory.
The Civil Service Commission does not concur in the recommendation.
WOODROW WILSON
THE WHITE HOUSE,
27 April, 1915.

Mrs. Lillian B. S. Grant may be reinstated to a position in the classi-
fied service in the Post Office Department, without regard to the length of
time she has been separated from the service.
Mrs. Grant, as Mrs. Lillie 11. Silcott wvas appointed to the position of
printer's assistant in the Bureau of Printing and Engraving on August 2
1895, and was promoted to operative and through the several grades of
that position. On July i, 1902-, she wvas transferred to the Post Office
Department as clerk at $900. and wvas promoted to $100o0 July i, 1905.
She resigned May 9, 191 2.
The Postmaster General advises that it is stated that Mrs. Grant's
husband is a permanent invalid, and that she is therefore compelled to pro-
vide a livelihood for both her husband and herself. In viewv of the cir-
cumstances and the fact that the records of the D~epartment showv that her
services were satisfactoiy and her duties faithfully discharged, the Post-
master General states that no objection would be offered by the Depart-
ment to the reinstatement of Mrs. Grant by Executive order.
The Civil Service Commission does not recommend the issuance of
an order in this case.
